properties.name: The cause of the skipped skill, measured: root-cause is demanded by no tool description and named by no trigger, and the project already measured that gap at 19-24 percent compliance
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL, ON REQUEST, 2026-09-07. Anthony ran /root-cause with the argument "your failure to obey the rule" after the agent had already offered two explanations without running it. This record supersedes the second of those; its central claim did not survive step 5.

STEP 1 - THE OBSERVATION, no diagnosis. rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed requires the root-cause skill on every issue a field report names. On the 2026-09-07 report the skill was not loaded. Tier 1 of the sibling rule ran and a cause was written from it. What is NOT affected: the ideas half of the same rule was followed in detail, and the rule's text had been read and its ruling recorded by the same agent hours earlier.

STEP 2 - PRECEDENT. The design holds req:the-reminder-rides-the-response ("a discipline the agent must hold across a long session rides the tool response it already reads, not prose it read once"), req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session, cap:skill-triggers and cap:skill-loads-are-counted. The question has been asked here before and instrumented.

STEP 3 - FOUR CANDIDATES, generated from the design rather than from memory:
(a) The agent did not know the rule.
(b) The skill was absent from context and the brainstorm skill was present, so the half with its text in front of the agent was followed.
(c) The trigger machinery that names skills does not name this one.
(d) The strongest lever the project has - a tool description that DEMANDS a skill - is unused for this skill.

STEP 4 AND 5 - THE MEASUREMENTS, taken 2026-09-07.
(a) REFUTED. The rule's full text was read and its enforcement ruling written the same session.
(b) REFUTED, and it was the agent's own previous answer. tools/loop_nudge.py names nine skills; the check-health skill is one of them and its text was also in context this session, and it was not run either, after more than thirty structural writes. Text in context is therefore not sufficient, so it cannot be the discriminating cause. The brainstorm half held for a reason outside the rule entirely: the USER had invoked /brainstorm earlier in the session for unrelated work, which put its text in front of the agent by luck rather than by design.
(c) CONFIRMED. Grepping the nudge for skill names: impact-check 10, link-artifacts 9, where-am-i 5, genesis 4, detect-and-ask 4, revise-design 1, check-health 1, capture-session 1, adopt 1. ROOT-CAUSE: ZERO. BRAINSTORM: ZERO. The two skills this rule mandates are precisely the two the trigger machinery never names. The nudge's own comment records the measured reason this matters: what predicts whether a skill gets loaded is being named in that string, and where-am-i, which is named there, is the most-loaded skill by a factor of 8.4.
(d) CONFIRMED, and it is the sharpest of the four. tools/skill_lint.py enforces a `demanded_by` declaration: a skill names the tools whose descriptions must name it back, so an agent calling the tool is told the skill exists. EXACTLY ONE SKILL IN THE PROJECT DECLARES IT - impact-check, demanded by record_change. root-cause declares none. The lint comment carries the measurement that made it the lever, over 91 sessions of a real project: record_change 19 percent, add_artifact 22 percent, add_change_event 24 percent, add_requirement 61 percent of sessions doing the work ever opened the matching skill. Between a third and four-fifths did not.

STEP 6 - THE CLASS, which is what makes this worth the record. The skipped skill is not the instance; the instance is that this agent skipped this skill on this report. The class is that ROOT-CAUSE'S TRIGGER IS THE ONLY ONE IN THE SET DEFINED BY THE AGENT'S OWN INTERNAL STATE. Its own text says so: the trigger is not a failure, it is the moment you are about to write down a cause. Every skill the nudge successfully names fires on something OBSERVABLE - a tool was called, a file was edited, a session started. There is no tool call for having formed an explanation, so there is nothing for a trigger to key on, and the skill is reachable only by an agent remembering to want it. Measured at 19-24 percent when nothing demands it. The agent's behaviour here is an instance inside that measured range, not an anomaly, which is the test the skill's step 6 asks for: would this fix have stopped the earlier occurrences? A rule restated more firmly would not. A demand on the tool would.

STEP 7 IS OWED AND NOT DONE. No test was written, because the fix is not built: the failing-first test belongs with the fix, and the fix is a code change inside dec:v0520-takes-the-field-feedback-triage-first-then-the-cement-measure. Stating this rather than quietly skipping it, because a fix without a failing-first test and one with it both end green.

STEP 8 - THE FIX, AT THE CAUSE. Writing a dated defect or finding TemporalFact IS the observable act of recording a cause - it is the moment the skill exists for, and it is a tool call. Today that act has no typed constructor at all; it goes through generic create_node, which is also another instance of declared vocabulary unreachable from the surface. So the fix is one change that closes two things: a typed constructor for recording a finding, whose description DEMANDS the root-cause skill by name, with root-cause declaring `demanded_by` on it so the lint holds it there. Naming root-cause in the nudge string is the cheaper second prong, and the design has already measured that channel at 8.4x.

STEP 9 - WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Whether a demand actually moves the load rate is an open experiment the lint comment says is running now, with baselines taken; this record assumes the lever works and that assumption is untested. The 19-24 percent figures are from one project's sessions, not from this agent. And nothing here establishes why root-cause and brainstorm were left out of the nudge - no decision in the record says it was deliberate, and the nudge's comment says the set was kept deliberately small because naming all 23 skills would recreate the catalogue that demonstrably does not predict loading. So adding root-cause to that string is a change with a stated cost, not a free win.
